Confidence decreases after day five; recheck the latest marine forecast before departure.

field_reports.name: Bayside Marine Monterey Bay Report
field_reports.summary: The fishing was good early in the morning for rock fish and sea bass. There were some good scores of sea bass caught near Pajaro and Davenport. The rock fish were on the bite near 4 Mile. The bonito and barracuda are being caught near Capitola. The warm water is still pushing up the coast and the year is far from over!

field_reports.name: Fishing the North Coast
field_reports.summary: fishingthenorthcoast October 1, 2026 Plenty of Fishing Options While We Wait for the Fall Rains Late fall kings, like the one pictured with angler Haley Richards while fishing the Chetco a couple years back, will begin to make their way into the coastal rivers once the winter rains begin. Photo courtesy of Brookings Fishing Charters. While we wait for fall rains to bring much-needed water to our rivers and usher in the late-fall Chinook salmon, the North Coast is far from short on angling options. Offshore, boat-based rockfish and lingcod season runs through Dec. 31, with fishing allowed at all depths. That lines up perfectly with the Nov. 7 sport Dungeness crab opener. Crab and rockfish combo trips are among the most popular outings on the North Coast, and anglers will want to take full advantage. Rockfish and federally managed groundfish fishing for divers and shore-based anglers is also allowed year-round, subject to current regulations. If you haven’t gotten your fill of Pacific halibut — and judging by the catch rates, many anglers haven’t — there’s still plenty of quota remaining. field_reports.name: Dockside Depoe Bay Daily Report
field_reports.summary: The Surfrider after a day off from bad weather yesterday had a really good day out on the water with the rockfish literally biting like "fleas". We had a real good catch for all folks onboard and some really good grade to the rockfish size. The Lingcod bite was a little off this morning from where it was earlier in the week but we did get some really nice ones like the one in the picture. Crabbing is still holding on with some good results as each passenger took home 8-per person. Looking at the forecast about a week out the ocean conditions look really good so give the Dockside office a call and get your name on the list for a bottom fish trip.

field_reports.name: Shake N' Bake Ilwaco Report
field_reports.summary: We had been hearing lousy reports from the commercial guys since the big storm passed through and we were wondering if the season might be ending. We ran 40 miles SW and had six in the box within the first 10 minutes and it never slowed up much. We chased birds and jumpers all day and left biting fish with 65 tuna. There were jumpers and birds everywhere. It looks like there is still quite a bit of fishing left this season. Mike C 9/26 slow full moon fishing.

field_reports.name: ODFW Ocean Salmon Updates
field_reports.mode: official commercial troll catch and management updates
field_reports.summary: Tomorrow's in-season call with NMFS and the State of Oregon, to discuss Oregon's (SOF) recreational ocean salmon fisheries is cancelled. For the 2026 recreational non-mark selective coho fishery from Cape Falcon to Humbug Mountain, the estimated catch through September 20, 2026, is approximately 22,250 coho salmon, or 87% of the 25,700 quota. The expected coho salmon catch for Saturday September 26, 2026, which was previously adopted and remains open as scheduled, does not provide sufficient balance to add any additional days to the fishery. PREVIOUS ACTION TAKEN: • Effective Saturday, September 26, 2026, from 12:01 a.m. through September 26, 2026, at 11:59 p.m., for the ocean recreational fishery from Cape Falcon to Humbug Mountain, retention of coho salmon is allowed, with a daily bag limit of two salmon (no fin clip requirement). Beginning Sunday, September 27, 2026, the season remains open through October 31, 2026, all salmon, except coho salmon, with a daily bag limit of two salmon. The minimum size for kept Chinook salmon is 24 inches in total length.
